nodes.content: Develop RLHF that preserves conflicting minority preferences under policy-induced distribution shifts without observing annotator group identities.
requirements: Improve worst-group preference win rate by ≥5 percentage points versus pooled RLHF, matching feedback budgets.
Establish identifiability conditions separating persistent preference disagreement from annotation noise under distribution shift.

nodes.content: Fit common-support latent-mixture rewards from anonymous multi-pair sessions with repeated anchors; optimize worst-component preference win rate under shifts.
How much anchor overlap and within-session repetition suffice to identify persistent latent preferences separately from annotation noise under policy-induced shifts?
Three conditionally independent anchor replicates identify opposing two-component preferences and symmetric flip noise under shared coverage and sub-50% error.
Derive three-view identifiability and label-swap limits, then simulate policy shifts varying anchor coverage (10–50%) and flip noise (5–45%).
In ShiftAnchor-Sim, compare component and noise recovery with two versus three independent anchor replicates across 10–50% coverage and 5–45% flips.
ShiftAnchor-Sim (30% coverage, 20% flips): three-view component MAE was 0.04 versus 0.09 for two views; noise MAE was 0.02.
Prioritize three-view anchor sessions over two-view designs; ShiftAnchor-Sim reduced component MAE from 0.09 to 0.04.
Using prioritized three-view anchors, derive rank and shared-support conditions for identifiability up to label swaps; construct zero-overlap counterexamples.
Three-View Identifiability Note v1 states full-rank anchor views and shared support suffice up to label swaps, with zero-overlap counterexamples.
Using Three-View Identifiability Note v1, run ShiftAnchor-Bench rank/overlap ablations and budget-matched worst-group win-rate comparisons against pooled RLHF.
ShiftAnchor-Bench (12,000 labels): worst-group win rate was 61% versus pooled RLHF’s 54%; zero-overlap and rank-deficient ablations scored 53% and 52%.
Using Three-View Identifiability Note v1, run budget-matched adaptive policy rollouts against pooled RLHF; unblind groups only for evaluation.
Adaptive ShiftAnchor-Bench rollouts (12,000 labels; 30% anchor coverage) yielded 50% worst-group win rate versus pooled RLHF’s 54%.
Does policy-induced context drift destroy conditional anchor overlap despite 30% aggregate coverage, explaining the 50% worst-group win rate?
Compare fixed versus adaptive ShiftAnchor-Bench (12,000 labels), correlating context-conditional anchor overlap and view rank with worst-group win rate.
Adaptive rollouts retained 30% aggregate anchors but had 3% minimum context-conditional overlap versus fixed rollouts’ 22%; worst-group wins fell 61%→50%.
Revise anchor sampling to enforce context-conditional overlap, since adaptive rollouts’ 3% minimum coincided with a drop to 50% worst-group wins.
ShiftGuard-RLHF allocates fixed-budget three-view anchors to maintain ≥20% context-conditional overlap and optimizes conservative worst-component win rates.
Can ShiftGuard-RLHF sustain ≥20% conditional overlap within 12,000 labels and exceed pooled adaptive worst-group wins by ≥5 points?
With 12,000 labels, ShiftGuard-RLHF maintains ≥20% minimum context-conditional overlap and reaches ≥59% worst-group win rate versus pooled RLHF’s 54%.
Run five-seed adaptive ShiftAnchor-Bench rollouts, budgeting 12,000 labels per method; compare conditional overlap and worst-group wins against pooled RLHF.
Across five 12,000-label adaptive rollouts, ShiftGuard-RLHF maintained 21% minimum conditional overlap and 60% worst-group wins versus pooled RLHF’s 54%.
Select ShiftGuard-RLHF for adaptive shifts: it achieved 60% versus pooled RLHF’s 54% worst-group wins at 12,000 labels.
PanelDRO-RLHF uses pseudonymous cross-policy recontact and randomized repeated comparisons to identify stable dissent, then optimizes pessimistic latent-profile win rates.
Can cross-policy recontact distinguish persistent dissent from session noise when annotator attrition depends on policy outputs?
With ≥15% recontact per history stratum and independent three-view repeats, PanelDRO identifies dissent; unobserved-preference-dependent attrition remains nonidentifiable.
On PanelAttrition-Sim, test PanelDRO’s three-view dissent recovery with ≥15% history-stratified recontact; construct observationally equivalent preference-dependent-attrition counterexamples.
PanelAttrition-Sim: despite 18% history-stratified recontact, three independent rank-deficient views left dissent unidentifiable even under history-conditional attrition.
Run PanelAttrition-Sim with full-rank versus rank-deficient three-view anchors at 18% recontact, crossing history-conditional and preference-dependent attrition; measure dissent-recovery error.
PanelAttrition-Sim: full-rank views at 18% recontact yielded 0.04 dissent MAE under history-conditional attrition; preference-dependent attrition remained nonidentifiable.
Can PanelDRO-RLHF achieve ≥59% worst-group wins within 12,000 labels while maintaining full-rank views and ≥15% recontact?
Compare PanelDRO’s worst-group wins against pooled RLHF on 12,000-label PanelAttrition-Bench with full-rank anchors, 18% recontact, and history-conditional attrition.
PanelAttrition-Bench v1 report records 59% PanelDRO versus 54% pooled worst-group wins at 12,000 labels, with anchor-rank diagnostics.
ProbeRoute-RLHF routes between two response policies using anonymous in-session choices; randomized repeated probes distinguish stable dissent from noise under shifts.
Can three randomized in-session probes reliably route between preference policies under adaptive shifts within a 12,000-label budget?
Three independent full-rank probes yield ≥80% routing accuracy and ≥59% worst-group wins under adaptive shifts using 12,000 labels.
Train latent-profile policies; randomize three independent full-rank session probes; evaluate routing accuracy and worst-group wins across 12,000-label adaptive rollouts.
Run five-seed ProbeRoute adaptive ShiftAnchor-Bench with 12,000 total labels including probes; audit routing accuracy and worst-group wins.
Five adaptive ShiftAnchor-Bench seeds: ProbeRoute achieved 82% routing accuracy and 60% worst-group wins versus pooled RLHF’s 54%, including probes.
Stress-test ProbeRoute’s successful three-probe configuration under correlated errors and context-specific rank loss; measure routing accuracy and worst-group wins.
At 10% correlated probe errors, full-rank ProbeRoute retained 59% worst-group wins versus pooled 54%; context-specific rank loss yielded 52%.
When do randomized in-session probes distinguish persistent preference conflict from correlated annotation noise without cross-session recontact?
Under full-rank probes, conditional error independence, and context overlap, shift-invariant dissent is identifiable; arbitrary shared-session noise is not.
Prove three-view identifiability under conditional independence and full-rank overlap; construct observationally equivalent shared-noise models and audit ProbeRoute contexts.
Three-view proof identified dissent under independent full-rank probes; observationally equivalent shared-noise models yielded 51% worst-group wins versus pooled 54%.
Can anonymous in-session probe routing preserve preferences when the minority profile represents only 5% of annotators?
Sweep 5–20% minority prevalence in five-seed, 12,000-label ProbeRoute rollouts; compare minority routing and worst-group wins against pooled RLHF.
Sweep 5–20% minority prevalence across five 12,000-label seeds; audit ProbeRoute probe rank, noise independence, minority routing, and worst-group wins.
At 5% minority prevalence, ProbeRoute achieved 68% minority routing and 51% worst-group wins versus pooled RLHF’s 47%.
Defer ProbeRoute for 5% minorities: its 51% worst-group win rate exceeds pooled RLHF by only 4 points, below target.
After deferral, test full-rank uncertainty-targeted probes at 5% prevalence with 12,000 labels, targeting ≥52% worst-group wins versus pooled’s 47%.
ProbeRoute-5% v2 report records 53% worst-group wins versus pooled RLHF’s 47% at 12,000 labels, with full-rank probe diagnostics.
